recent_posts.title: Introducing IBM StockTrader
recent_posts.summary: IBM Stock Trader is a simple stock trading sample, where you can create various stock portfolios and add shares of stock to each for a commission. It keeps track of each portfolio’s total value and its loyalty level, notifying you of changes in level, which affect the commission charged per transaction. The concept demonstrates how to run a microservices-based application in a Kubernetes environment.

recent_posts.title: Learn best practices for debugging and error handling in an enterprise-grade blockchain application
recent_posts.summary: Blockchain is a shared, replicated immutable ledger for recording transactions, tracking assets, and building trust. It is built on properties like consensus, provenance, immutability, finality. This blog post focuses on different points of failures in a typical blockchain-based application, possible reasons for failures, and recommended debugging and error handling techniques.

recent_posts.title: How fuzzing can make your open-source project more secure and reliable
recent_posts.summary: Fuzzing analyzes the vulnerability of software through programmatic code testing. Fuzzing helps uncover programming errors in software that cannot possibly be captured otherwise. etcd is a critical component of Kubernetes where it is used as the primary data store for cluster data.

recent_posts.title: Egeria Dojos and the IBM Developer community
recent_posts.summary: Egeria is an open source project under LF AI & Data that provices open metadata and governance for enterprises. It automatically captures, manages, and exchanges metadata between tools and platforms in a vendor-neutral way. Each tool is linked through an integration service that is tailored for that specific type of tool.

recent_posts.title: Knative joins the CNCF as a serverless incubation project
recent_posts.summary: IBM joins the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) and the Knative community in welcoming Knative as the newest incubating project. This important milestone is crucial for the future of Knative and the CNCF. IBM is currently involved in improving Knative’s performance, async calls, and leading the Knatives operator.

recent_posts.title: Take control of your change request workflow with the IBM Cloud reference implementation of DevSecOps
recent_posts.summary: Change management can be a useful risk mitigation tool and has evolved to be a core component of cloud-native application development processes. IBM found its own answers to these challenges with standardized, integrated, and automated DevSecOps best practices. The reference implementation is built on the IBM Cloud Continuous Delivery service, which provides Git repos and issue tracking.

recent_posts.title: Red Hat OpenShift Serverless on IBM Power
recent_posts.summary: Red Hat OpenShift Serverless streamlines the process of delivering code from development to production. It eliminates the need for developers to understand the underlying architecture or manage back-end hardware configurations to run their software. Developers can use a single platform for hosting their microservices, legacy, and serverless applications.

recent_posts.title: Julia is now supported on IBM Power
recent_posts.summary: Julia is a general-purpose programming language with a special focus on scientific computing. Julia is as fast as C programming language in many cases while remaining dynamic like Python. Julia 1.6.2 is supported on the IBM Power platform, “Tier-3” level.

recent_posts.title: What you need to know about WebSphere Hybrid Edition
recent_posts.summary: IBM WebSphere Hybrid Edition is a bundle of IBM runtimes for enterprise and cloud-native Java workloads. Liberty is a fast, lightweight, and modular framework for cloud- native Java applications and microservices that are optimized for cloud and Kubernetes. WebSphere Application Migration Toolkit assists developers to make code changes to modernize their Java applications.

recent_posts.title: IBM homomorphic encryption: A DASHing solution for healthcare data privacy
recent_posts.summary: In 2021, our team won third place in the second track of the iDASH workshop challenge on healthcare data privacy. Our solution classified 2000 viruses in less than 1 second with more than 99% accuracy. The DNA sequences were encoded and encrypted using the client’s key, with each team providing software that simulated the client.

top_posts.title: 6 developer trends to watch in 2021
top_posts.summary: IBM developer advocates share their thoughts on what they see as a major trend for 2021. Data privacy in security is one of the top trends for 2021, according to IBM. Chatbots are going to be something that is requested this year, says IBM developer advocate Hana Ibrahim. We’ve moved beyond the hype cycle for DevOps, DevSecOps, and Data Ops.

top_posts.title: 6-year-old Guinness World Record programmer completes IBM AI certification
top_posts.summary: Kautilya Katariya of Northampton, U.K., was recently granted a programming Guinness World Record at the age of 6 years and 346 days old. Courses from the IBM Developer Skills Network helped make this possible. Developers of any age who are seeking to advance their skills — especially in AI — can earn several new professional certificates.

top_posts.title: Node.js 15 release: Updated handling of rejections, npm 7, N-API Version 7, and more
top_posts.summary: The Node.js community is releasing Node.JS 15 with new features that are important to users and customers. It won’t be promoted to long-term support (LTS), but we need our customers and the greater ecosystem to try it out and give us feedback. Some of the new features and ongoing work in the 15 release include:Updated handling of rejections. Refinement of the Async Local Storage APIs.

top_posts.title: Next generation of IBM C/C++ and Fortran compilers are now available on IBM AIX
top_posts.summary: IBM Open XL C/C++ and Fortran compilers provide differentiating values for IBM Power10 hardware both on premises and in hybrid cloud. The new IBM Open XL compilers can take advantage of both common LLVM optimizations and IBM’s advanced optimizations, increasing general performance for workloads.

top_posts.title: Node.js Reference Architecture: Logging in Node.js
top_posts.summary: The Node.js Reference Architecture recommends Pino as a great tool for logging in your Node.JS application. The article concludes by walking you through an example of logging in a node.js application in production. Understanding what tools to use for logging is a critical step to ensuring they run well in production, says IBM.
